data.source_title: The effect of emergency department crowding on reassessment of children with critically abnormal vital signs
data.locator: Abstract, Methods and Results; triage vital-sign reassessment, electronic alert after 1 hour.
data.source_setting: Pediatric ED at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center; patients placed in regular ED rooms after critically abnormal triage vital signs.
data.source_n: 9,976 patients with critically abnormal triage vital signs among 253,408 visits (3.9%).
data.quantity: Mean time to repeat vital signs and association between crowding and reassessment rate
data.unit: minutes; relative reassessment rate per 10 patients
data.source_evidence_basis: Retrospective cross-sectional cohort, Cox time-to-event analysis; electronic alerts prompted reassessment after one hour. Crowding correlated with slower reassessment.
data.limitations: Pediatric single-center retrospective study; sample restricted to patients with critically abnormal triage vitals placed in regular rooms, not all waiting-room arrivals. Association does not establish causation or a staffing standard.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent waiting after triage as an active monitored state with a reassessment due event and escalation pathway; test missed/delayed reassessment under congestion without borrowing a RWJ interval or probability.
